items.grounds: Re-derived both ways. MT 66:18 opens "וְאָנֹכִ֗י מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ וּמַחְשְׁבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם בָּאָ֕ה" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier); the verse carries no form of the root 'know' at any tier (skeleton sweep of the yod-dalet-ayin / dalet-ayin consonant runs: 66:18 absent from both hit-lists), so WEB's “For I know their works and their thoughts.” (web:Isa.66.18) supplies a verb the MT does not have, and its 'For' renders the conjunctive waw of "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier). The shipped boundary_evidence_refs carry web:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18 with no oshb:Isa.66.18 counterpart, and the row's stated reason for closing ('The unit ends there because 66:18 opens with a first-person emphatic pivot') is warranted by that WEB run alone -- a boundary-relevant Hebrew form claim carried by a translation rendering (E-23 / engagement class). Against the finding: the pivot itself is byte-true -- "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier) is the verse-initial 1cs independent pronoun, a verse-initial anokhi/ve-anokhi token standing in 8 verses book-wide (sweep: 8 verses, word-bound token, skeleton tier: 43:11, 43:12, 43:25, 45:12, 45:13, 51:12, 51:15, 66:18) -- and the auditor's 'sole rear-seam driver' overstates: the rear seam also rests on the verse-final signature "נְאֻם יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.17, byte tier) (word-bound verse-final in 6 verses book-wide, sweep: 6 verses, skeleton tier), which the row cites at byte tier. So the seam survives; what fails is the warrant, translation-carried for a Hebrew claim, with the WEB run misdescribing the MT clause. Defective warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium confirmed. The proposed non-span remedy (add oshb:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18 and carry the pivot on a pointed splice of "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier)) is byte-sound.

Re-derived. MT 66:15 opens "כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ יָב֔וֹא" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier); MT 66:14 closes "וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת אֹיְבָֽיו" (oshb:Isa.66.14, byte tier); MT 66:16 chains "כִּ֤י בָאֵשׁ֙" (oshb:Isa.66.16, byte tier). The connective is byte-true and its backward force is content-real: 66:14b already states the judgment on 'his enemies' inside the preceding row, and "כִּֽי" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier) subordinates the fire-theophany of 66:15-16 to that clause as its explication -- so the row's front-seam warrant ('a register shift from the maternal-comfort imagery of the preceding unit into universal judgment') mislocates the register turn by half a verse, and the counter-signal is disclosed nowhere in the row (the gloss 'for behold' names the particle but never its continuity force). Against the finding, calibration: verse-initial ki opens 115 verses book-wide (sweep: 115 verses, word-bound token, skeleton tier; in this chapter 66:12, 66:15, 66:16, 66:22), so the connective alone distinguishes nothing at any seam here; and the specific onset pair "כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier) is verse-initial in exactly 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier: 3:1, 26:21, 60:2, 66:15), each an announcement onset (26:21 the closest theophany parallel), so the row's onset reading is well-founded and the seam is defensible: the 66:12-14 declaration closes syntactically on its own weqatal chain "וְנוֹדְעָ֤ה יַד יְהוָה֙" (oshb:Isa.66.14, byte tier) ... "וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת אֹיְבָֽיו" (oshb:Isa.66.14, byte tier), and 66:15 opens on the presentative with YHWH as explicit subject. No merge; no mark at MT 66:14 or 66:15 in the parashah inventory (single witness) bears either way. Defective warrant not alone load-bearing (cross-seam cohesion rule, undisclosed and unrebutted): medium confirmed; the proposed one-clause disclosure in device_notes or the rejected alternative is the correct non-span cure.

Dependent on the two seam items, both confirmed at medium from bytes: the rear seam's stated closing reason is warranted by a WEB run only, with no oshb:Isa.66.18 ref and the MT lacking the verb the run supplies (MT 66:18 opens "וְאָנֹכִ֗י מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ וּמַחְשְׁבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם בָּאָ֕ה" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier)); the front seam carries the undisclosed backward-linking "כִּֽי" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier) of 66:15 bound to "וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת אֹיְבָֽיו" (oshb:Isa.66.14, byte tier) in 66:14. The parashah inventory (single witness) places this chapter's marks at MT 66:4, 66:9 and 66:11 only (all SAMEKH), none at MT 66:14, 66:15, 66:17 or 66:18, so both seams rest on tier-1 signals alone, as the row's own device_notes concede; the one K/Q note the inventory carries in this span (MT 66:17, 1 note) is correctly disclosed. The neighbouring row spanning Isa.66.12-Isa.66.14 carries the identical Isa.66.14|Isa.66.15 seam on the same theophany-onset driver at 'medium'. A 'high' band over a seam pair with one translation-carried warrant and one unrebutted continuity signal outruns the warrants as shipped; the span is not a whole chapter, so the chapter-fallback cap is not the mechanism. Medium confirmed (a defective calibration claim, not load-bearing); reduction to 'medium' is the remedy as shipped, re-openable only if both seam warrants are repaired.

Re-derived both ways. MT 66:23 closes on "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier): the two-token pair's consonantal skeleton stands in 53 verses book-wide and word-bound verse-final in exactly 5 (sweep: 53 verses / 5 verse-final, skeleton tier: 39:6, 54:1, 65:25, 66:21, 66:23) -- the row's digits and the auditor's re-sweep both confirmed. MT 66:24 opens "וְיָצְא֣וּ וְרָא֔וּ" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier). The finding's core is correct: the row's two stated reasons for holding the couplet (the terminal-span tiling fact; the internal turn being 'a distinct rhetorical function from the ingathering report that precedes it') distinguish the couplet from 66:18-22 but bind nothing across 66:23|66:24, and the row computes the verse-final closure signal at 66:23 without applying the addressee/frame/scene test its neighbour applies at 66:21. Defective cohesion warrant: medium confirmed. Against the finding, the respan case fails on bytes: 66:24's 3mp verbs "וְיָצְא֣וּ וְרָא֔וּ" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) carry NO expressed subject -- every plural noun in the verse sits inside the prepositional phrase "בְּפִגְרֵי֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַפֹּשְׁעִ֖ים בִּ֑י" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) -- so their antecedent is "כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) in 66:23 (the worshippers who come are those who go out and see), the weqatal sequence "יָב֧וֹא כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) ... "וְיָצְא֣וּ וְרָא֔וּ" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) runs across the verse boundary despite the intervening signature, and 66:24 closes verse-finally on "וְהָי֥וּ דֵרָא֖וֹן לְכָל בָּשָֽׂר" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier), so the all-flesh collocation frames the couplet at its only adjacent-verse pair in the book (word-bound collocation: 5 verses book-wide, sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier: 40:5, 49:26, 66:16, 66:23, 66:24). The auditor's 'fresh scene with a new subject' is therefore not byte-grounded on the subject limb. Span ruling: decline_proposal -- option (a) would sever a subjectless weqatal continuation from its antecedent and split the collocation frame; option (b), retaining Isa.66.23-Isa.66.24 and stating the anaphoric-subject plus all-flesh-frame warrant in place of the tiling fact, is a non-span repair and is the sound cure. The coda-versus-close question the row holds open is book-level, but the 66:23|66:24 binding is resolved below it, so no book-level deferral.

Re-swept. The consonantal-substring sweep underlying "כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) returns 6 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses, 6 token occurrences, skeleton tier: 22:13, 40:5, 49:26, 66:16, 66:23, 66:24). The 22:13 hit spans the tail of the infinitive and the following noun in "אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר" (oshb:Isa.22.13, byte tier) ('eat meat'), not the all-flesh collocation; and the articular site "כָּל הַבָּשָׂ֣ר" (oshb:Isa.40.6, byte tier) is excluded because its skeleton carries the article. Word-bound, the collocation proper stands in 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier: 40:5, 49:26, 66:16, 66:23, 66:24; 66:24 with the lamed prefix "לְכָל בָּשָֽׂר" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier)) plus the articular 40:6 site as a separately named object. So the shipped '6 book-wide' names 'the all-flesh collocation' but counts a substring census that includes a non-collocation site and omits an attested articular one -- a blended count object on a two-letter head word, the class the hazard catalog requires word-binding for; the tier is honestly named but the object is not. The in-chapter digit re-verifies exactly both ways (3 verses: "כָּל בָּשָׂ֑ר" (oshb:Isa.66.16, byte tier), "כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier), "לְכָל בָּשָֽׂר" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier)). Sits in device_notes supporting the held coda question, not either seam: defective digit not load-bearing, medium confirmed; either restatement in the proposed change cures it.
